# Finance (No. 2) Act 2010

## Overview

The Finance (No. 2) Act 2010 is a United Kingdom Act of Parliament that received Royal Assent on **27 July 2010**. It was introduced by the newly formed Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government following the May 2010 general election.

## Key Provisions

### Capital Gains Tax
- Increased the higher rate of Capital Gains Tax from **18% to 28%** for higher and additional rate taxpayers
- The 18% rate was retained for basic rate taxpayers

### Bank Levy
- Introduced a new **bank levy** targeting the balance sheets of UK banks and building societies
- Aimed at ensuring the banking sector made a contribution reflecting the risks it posed to the financial system

### Corporation Tax
- Announced plans to reduce the main rate of Corporation Tax (implemented over subsequent years)
- Small profits rate was also addressed

### VAT
- Confirmed the increase in **VAT from 17.5% to 20%**, effective from January 2011

### Income Tax
- Maintained the 50% additional rate of income tax introduced by the previous government

## Context

This was an emergency budget measure reflecting the coalition's austerity agenda to address the UK's deficit following the 2008 financial crisis. It was George Osborne's first budget as Chancellor of the Exchequer.
